concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: Asymptotic upper bounds on running time.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Sums of coefficients times powers of a variable, with addition and multiplication.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a+bi with i²=-1, including roots of unity.

concepts.name: Multitape Turing machine
concepts.gloss: A Turing machine with finitely many tapes, a fixed alphabet, and one cell read/written per tape per step.

concepts.name: Discrete Fourier transform and cyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: The DFT maps a length-q sequence to averages weighted by roots of unity; it turns cyclic convolution into pointwise multiplication.

evidence.quote: (F_q u)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}u_j e^{-2\pi i jk/q}

Here $*$ denotes
cyclic convolution on the product of the coordinate groups

concepts.name: The n log n conjecture and prior multiplication algorithms
concepts.gloss: Schönhage–Strassen proposed n log n as optimal multiplication time; Harvey and van der Hoeven reached O(n log n).

evidence.quote:
Harvey and van der Hoeven reached the unconditional $O(n\log n)$ upper
bound
proposed $n\log n$ as the optimal order of growth

concepts.name: O(n log n) multiplier as a subroutine
concepts.gloss: The established Harvey–van der Hoeven fixed-tape integer multiplier, called as an ordinary subroutine on short inputs.

evidence.quote:
Calls to the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier are ordinary subroutine
calls
This is an independent subroutine.

concepts.name: Multiplication as convolution of radix digits
concepts.gloss: Splitting inputs into radix digits turns integer multiplication into convolution of short integer coefficient lists, later carried back to the binary product by carries.

evidence.quote:
Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to
convolution of short integer coefficients.

propagates carries to
obtain the exact binary product

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder map to prime cyclic axes
concepts.gloss: The coefficient list is placed on a product of distinct prime cyclic axes by a Chinese-remainder map preserving convolution.

evidence.quote:
placed on a product of
distinct prime cyclic axes by a Chinese-remainder map that preserves
convolution

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: Harvey–van der Hoeven technique expressing a Fourier transform of coprime length through a power-of-two transform, here keeping the two coordinate permutations inside the transform formula.

evidence.quote:
Gaussian
resampling connects these two shapes.

We retain both permutations in the transform formula and
compute that formula directly.

concepts.name: Bluestein chirp identity
concepts.gloss: Converts a Fourier transform, including its target permutation, into a cyclic convolution with pointwise phase multiplications.

evidence.quote:
Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform,
including its target permutation, into normalized cyclic convolution.

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r + 1$

symbols.name: ring variable
symbols.meaning: The formal variable of the polynomials; its powers act as roots of unity.

symbols.name: coefficient count
symbols.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a polynomial record, a power of two.

concepts.gloss: Complex polynomials modulo y^r+1 with r a power of two, in which multiplying by a power of y is a signed shift of the coefficient list.

evidence.quote: \mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)

multiplication
by such a root is a signed shift of the coefficient list

concepts.name: Two-point butterfly
concepts.title: Two-point butterfly $H_0$

symbols.name: butterfly map
symbols.meaning: The map sending a pair (u,v) to ((u+v)/2,(u−v)/2).

concepts.gloss: The map (u,v)↦((u+v)/2,(u−v)/2) applied to a pair of values; the building block of fast transforms.

evidence.quote: H_0(u,v)=\bigl((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2\bigr)

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transforms
concepts.gloss: Fourier transforms over the ring modulo y^r+1 using powers of y as roots of unity, so root multiplications are signed shifts, evaluated by butterfly layers with a retained frequency order.

evidence.quote:
Powers of $y$ then
serve as roots of unity in the remaining axes

These are the
synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle

concepts.name: Signed packing (Kronecker substitution)
concepts.gloss: Multiplying ring polynomials exactly by packing signed coefficients into one integer, calling the integer multiplier, and unpacking.

evidence.quote:
Their polynomial products
use signed packing and the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier as an
ordinary subroutine.

The
reduction is a signed form of Kronecker substitution

concepts.name: Fixed-point precision, exact dyadics and error control
concepts.gloss: Values are complex numbers on a 2^-p grid; intermediate arithmetic is exact over Gaussian dyadics, with a single truncation, and total error is kept below 1/2 so rounding recovers integers.

evidence.quote: Intermediate values are exact Gaussian dyadics

proves that the recovered
coefficient error is strictly below $1/2$

concepts.name: Arrays on tape, address fields and volume
concepts.gloss: Arrays are stored in lexicographic order with implicit addresses split into fields; volume V is the number of stored data bits; permutations are realized by scans.

evidence.quote:
An array with address set $[a_1]\times\cdots\times[a_t]$ is stored in
lexicographic order
The \emph{logical volume} $V$ is the number of stored data bits.

concepts.name: Linear networks, roles and frames
concepts.gloss: A fixed linear network of gates exchanges two banks of values with signs and restores auxiliary values; roles are wire places and frames are invertible operators giving the stored representation, cancelling so the endpoint operator is the desired one.

evidence.quote:
A wire's fixed place in the network
is called its role.

We call $D_v$ its frame: the stored
array is $D_vg$ when the logical array is $g$.

concepts.name: Finite networks from three-element subsets
concepts.gloss: Construction using three-element subsets, gather, scatter and scratch wires, with nested subspaces at vertices so that the total number of smaller calls is below the number of roles times m.

evidence.quote:
The construction uses
three-element subsets: gather and scatter create coefficients depending
on intersection size, and auxiliary wires cancel the unwanted
coefficients.
Let $\mathcal T$ be the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$.

concepts.name: Recursive power saving s < Wm
concepts.title: Recursive saving $s<Wm$

symbols.name: smaller call count
symbols.meaning: The total number of smaller recursive calls used by the network.

symbols.name: role count
symbols.meaning: The number of wire roles among which rows are distributed.

symbols.name: parameter multiplier
symbols.meaning: The factor by which the recursion parameter grows in one level, the dimension of the fixed space.

concepts.gloss: Using s calls at parameter f on volume V/W each, with s<Wm, makes the cost per volume grow by a factor below m when the parameter is multiplied by m, giving a power rather than linear growth.

evidence.quote:
The decisive property is that the total
number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.

This strict inequality
is the source of the power saving.

concepts.name: Lower triangular factorization and address shear
concepts.gloss: Any rational matrix factors as lower-triangular times partial permutation times lower-triangular, so edge operators and address shears (H,D)↦(H+D,D) can be done in tape order at cost scaling with rank.

evidence.quote: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ has a factorization
updated by $(H,D)\mapsto(H+D,D)$

concepts.name: Fast address-chunk interchange
concepts.title: Address-chunk interchange in time $O(Vu^\tau)$

symbols.name: stored bit volume
symbols.meaning: The number of data bits stored in the array.

symbols.name: field width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each address field being interchanged.

concepts.gloss: Interchanging two disjoint address fields of u bits in an array of volume V in time O(V u^τ) with τ<1, via XOR combinations of intermediate data that finally give an exact permutation.

evidence.quote: Its cost is $O(Vu^\tau)$ for a fixed $\tau<1$.

intermediate
steps form pointwise XOR combinations of data

concepts.name: Fast simultaneous butterfly layers
concepts.title: Simultaneous butterfly layer in time $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$

symbols.name: stored bit volume
symbols.meaning: The number of data bits stored in the array.

symbols.name: chunk count
symbols.meaning: The number of equal-width address chunks whose selected bit is butterflied.

concepts.gloss: Applying the butterfly on the same bit position of up to d address chunks at once, on complex polynomial records, in time O(V d^λ') with λ'<1, instead of d whole-array passes.

evidence.quote:
the cost is $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ for a
fixed $\lambda'<1$

whereas separate butterfly
factors would require $D$ whole-array passes

concepts.name: Assembly of the integer multiplication algorithm
concepts.gloss: The pipeline: digits, Chinese-remainder prime axes, Gaussian resampling, chirp convolution, phase twist to the ring modulo y^r+1, synthetic transforms with fast layers, then rescaling, rounding and carries.

evidence.quote: Figure~\ref{fig:multiplication-flow} summarizes these reductions.

A compatible choice of rational
parameters makes all terms in its cost table fit Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.

concepts.name: Integer multiplication in O(n (lg n)^(1−κ)) time
concepts.title: Integer multiplication in time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$

symbols.name: input bit length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits of each integer operand.

symbols.name: saving exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed constant 2^{-182} giving the power saving in the logarithmic factor.

concepts.gloss: A deterministic multitape Turing machine multiplies n-bit integers in O(n(lg n)^(1−κ)) time with κ=2^-182, refuting the n log n optimality conjecture in this model.

evidence.quote: Its worst-case running time satisfies

disproves the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture
of Sch\"onhage and Strassen in this model

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic and residue rings
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on integers modulo m, with addition and multiplication of residue classes.

concepts.name: Prime numbers and coprimality
concepts.gloss: Primes are integers greater than 1 with no proper divisors, and two integers are coprime when their greatest common divisor is 1.

concepts.name: Binary representation of integers
concepts.gloss: A nonnegative integer is written as a sum of bits times powers of two, and n-bit integers have n such digits.

concepts.name: Matrices, linear maps and rank
concepts.gloss: Linear maps are represented by matrices, with rank the dimension of the image and invertibility meaning an inverse map exists.

concepts.name: Permutations
concepts.gloss: A permutation is a bijective reordering of a finite set of positions.

concepts.name: Logarithms and exponents
concepts.gloss: lg n is the base-2 logarithm and powers of two and their logarithms obey the usual identities.

concepts.name: Recurrences and divide and conquer
concepts.gloss: Running times of recursive algorithms are described by recurrences solved by unrolling or standard theorems.

concepts.name: Fast Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: The O(N log N) divide-and-conquer algorithm for the discrete Fourier transform of length N, built from butterfly steps.

concepts.name: Karatsuba and schoolbook multiplication
concepts.gloss: Elementary integer multiplication algorithms taking quadratic and about n^1.585 time respectively.

concepts.name: Floating-point and rounding errors
concepts.gloss: Approximate real arithmetic incurs bounded rounding errors that can be added using the triangle inequality, and rounding to the nearest integer recovers an integer when the error is below 1/2.

concepts.name: Sets, products and tuples
concepts.gloss: Finite sets, Cartesian products of index ranges, subsets, tuples and lexicographic ordering of tuples.

concepts.name: Linear-time scanning of tapes
concepts.gloss: A Turing machine can copy, compare, add and subtract integers by sequential passes over its tapes in linear time.

concepts.name: Asymptotic constants and small epsilon exponents
concepts.gloss: Constants independent of n may be absorbed in big-O, and exponents slightly below one distinguish polylogarithmic growth rates.

background.summary: The reader has completed undergraduate computer science: asymptotic analysis, discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, primes, basic number theory, finite sets, permutations), linear algebra over the reals and complex numbers (matrices, rank, invertibility, linear maps), and basic algorithm design including recursion, divide and conquer, recurrences, and the standard school and Karatsuba multiplication. They know Turing machines and tapes and probably the FFT as an algorithm, but not abstract algebra beyond basics, finite fields in depth, or any research-level multiplication algorithm.
